full_judgment:
Md Ashraful Kamal J : This Criminal Appeal was registered at the instance of the convict appellant ATM Qamruzzaman Khan against the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 14-5-2008 passed by the Special Judge, Special Court No. 2, Dhaka in Special Case No. 16 of 2007 convicting the appellant and another Md Atiq Ullah Khan Masud under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 read with section 109 of the Penal Code and sentencing them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a period of 7(seven) years and to pay a fine of Taka 1,22,44,2007 in equal share and in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment 1 (one) year more. 

 3. After recording of the First Information Report the charge of the investigation was entrusted to Md Abul Kashem (PW-10), the Deputy Assistant Director, Anti Corruption Commission, Head Office, Dhaka. On getting the responsibility, Md Abul Kashem visited the place of occurrence, prepared the sketch map with index, examined the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, interrogated the accused Md Atiqullah Khan Masud, taking approval from the Court and seized the alamots. After concluding the investigation, the investigating officer having found prima-facie case against the appellant along with Md Atiq Ullah Khan Masud, submitted charge-sheet under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 read with section 109 of the Penal Code. 

 4. Thereafter, the case record was transmitted to the Mohanagar Senior Special Judge, Dhaka for trial. Subsequently, the case record was transferred to the Special Judge, Special Judge Court No. 2, Dhaka, who on 6-1-2008 framed charge under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 read with section 109 of the Penal Code, 1860 against the appellant and Md Atiq Ullah Khan Masud. The charge was duly read over to accused Md Atiq Ullah Khan Masud and to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. But the charge could not read over to the appellant ATM Qumruzzaman Khan as he was abscond. 

 5. In this case prosecution examined as many as 10 witnesses and defence examined none. On closing of the evidence of the prosecution the convict appellant Md Atiq Ullah Khan Masud was examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure where he again pleaded innocence. On the other hand, the present appellant ATM Qumruzzaman Khan was abscond. 

 8. Mr Moin Uddin, the learned Advocate appearing for the convict appellant submits that after change of the Government in 2001, the present appellant was illegally removed from his service by RAJUK. Thereafter, the appellant filed Title Suit No. 271 of 2004 for declaration with regard that the removal of the appellant was illegal. That on 6-8-2007 the said suit was decreed in favour of the present appellant. Next, he submits that the appellant was implicated in the present case falsely to frustrate the aforesaid judgment and decree. His further contention is that the alleged occurrence took place between on 19-4-1999 to 23-5-1999 but the FIR was lodged on 9-8-2007 long after 9 (nine) years without giving any explanation. He finally submits that as per section 17 of the Building Construction Act, 1952 no proceeding shall lie against the government servant in respect of anything done in good faith. 

 9. Mr Bashir Ahmed along with Mr Md. Masud Hasan Chowdhury and Mr Kazi Md Mahmudul Karim (Ratan) learned Assistant Attorneys General appearing on behalf of the state, on the other hand, submits that the prosecution has able to prove their charge perfectly and all the 10(ten) witnesses categorically supported the prosecution case to the hilt and prays that the present appeal should be dismissed in all fairness. 

 11. Md Mahmood Hasan, Deputy Assistant Director as PW-1 in his examination-in-chief stated that he was the informant of the present case. He stated that 

 16. Md Aminur Rahman, Authorized Officer- 1 as PW-4 in his examination-in-chief stated that on 2-9-2007 at about 2 PM investigation officer of the present case came to the Authorized Officer room No. 4 and seized some documents and he was present over there and he signed the seizure list accordingly. He proved the seizure list as Exhibit-4 and his signature therein as Exhibit-4/2. He also proved the material Exhibit-I series. 

 17. Vobatush Bowmik, Sub-Registrar, Sadar Record Room, Tejgaon, Dhaka as PW-5 in his examination-in-chief stated that on 24-9-2007 investigation officer of this case came to his office and took the photocopy of the two powers of Attorney. He also stated that he gave report in respect of the said deeds. He proved the report as Exhibit-6 series and his signature therein as Exhibit-6/Ka series. 

 20. Abdur Rashid, Senior Deputy Manager of the Globe construction limited as PW-7 in his examination-in-chief stated that on 11-9-2007 he went to Anti-Corruption Office along with store keeper Md Rafiqur Rahman to meet the investigation officer Abul Kashem. He further stated that the investigation officer of this case prepared the seizure list in his presence and he signed in the seizure list as witness. He proved the seizure list and his signature therein as Exhibit-7 and 7/1. He also proved the seized alamot as material Exhibit-2. He also proved the 2nd seizure list and his signature therein as Exhibit-8 and 8/1. He proved the material Exhibit-6. 

 32. Notwithstanding, it further appears to us that as per section 15 of the ইমারত নির্মান বিধিমালা ১৯৫২ if any person is aggrieved by any order passed by any authorized officer under section 3 of the said Ain, he/she can prefer an appeal before the person designated or authority within 30 (thirty) days. But in the present case no one went to the appellate authority against the decision taken on 23-5-1999 by this appellant. Even though, RAJUK itself till today neither took any step nor set-aside the said decision of the present appellant in question. 

 33. FIR was lodged against the present convict appellant under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 read with section 109 of the Penal Code. Thereafter investigating officer after completion of the investigation found prima-facie case against the present appellant under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. After that Special Judge, Court No. 2, Dhaka on 6-1-2008 framed charge against the present appellant under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. And the Special Judge, Special Judge Court No. 2, Dhaka convicted the present appellant under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. 

 "Any public servant who commits or attempts to commit criminal misconduct shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both and the pecuniary resources or property to which the criminal misconduct relates may also be confiscated to the state." 

 35. On perusal of Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 it is evident that the section relates to public servant who commits or attempts to commit criminal misconduct. Now we see, what is criminal misconduct. Section 5(1) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 explain the Criminal Misconduct, which runs as follows:- 

 5. Criminal Misconduct—(1) "A public servant is said to commit the offence of criminal misconduct — 

 36. In light of the above provision of law, to convict a public servant under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, there must be ingredients of criminal misconduct as per section 5(1) of the Act. But in the present case, none of the prosecution witnesses stated anything about any criminal misconduct which was done by the appellant by approving the plan in question. 

 37. Apart from that this appellant neither has any relation to the convict Mr Md Atiq Ullah Khan Masud nor prosecution produced or proved any documents or evidences in respect of giving any bribe to the appellant by Md Atiq Ullah Khan Masud. Therefore, it is very difficult to understand how the present appellant committed criminal misconduct as enunciated in section 5(1) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. 

 38. Criminal misconduct cannot be assigned to any action of a public servant when he performs his function in accordance with the prescribed set of rules and procedures without manifestly showing any instance of abuse of his official position. 

 40. In this case, we are unable to find any-thing that the appellant had any criminal intent in taking the decision to approve the plan in question. Most interestingly, in the present case no one incurred any loss or suffered on account of the decision passed by the appellant on 23-5-1999. 

 43. Moreover, the case was started without any prior sanction for lodging the case against the appellant and the so-called sanction letter issued by the Commission for submitting charge-sheet was not in accordance with law and, as such, the mandatory provision of law has been violated in lodging the FIR or in starting the case against the appellant and, as such, it is ex facie illegal and amounts to a malice in law. 

 44. Furthermore, the occurrence took place on 23-5-1999, but the FIR was lodged on 9-8-2007. The absence of any satisfactory and reasonable explanation of such long delay creates ample doubt about the truthfulness of the prosecution case. 

 45. Significantly as well, we do not find anything from the record that the appellant by performing his function as an authorized officer committed any wrong or violated any provision of Building Construction Rules or Ain. We have also examined the statements of 10 (ten) witnesses adduced by the prosecution, but are unable to find any ingredients of the offence of criminal misconduct against the appellant punishable under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act. 

 49. In the above facts and circumstances and considering the above mandatory provision of law and by taking all the evidences cumulatively it cannot be said that the guilt of the convict appellant has been proved beyond a shadow of doubt and accordingly, we are of the opinion that this appeal has substance and that the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond a reasonable doubt. 

 51. In the result, the appeal is allowed. The judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 14-5-2008 passed by the Special Judge, Special Court No. 2, Dhaka is Special Case No. 16 of 2007 is hereby set aside as against the convict appellant ATM Qamruzzaman Khan son of Md. Nowsher Ali Khan as he is found not guilty of the charge brought against him and he be acquitted from the charge leveled against him.
